https://telex.hu/after/2026/08/04/m1-hir.text: Menü Kereső Magyar Péter kommentje után visszavonta a közmédia vezetősége Hajdú Gábor és Borsa Miklós megbízatását After Iván-Nagy Szilvia „Az M1 Híradó bejelentett főszerkesztőjének és műsorvezetőjének: Hajdú Gábornak és Borsa Miklósnak megbízását visszavonta a közmédia vezetősége. A megújuló közmédia hírszolgáltatásának a társadalom bizalmát vissza kell állítania” – jelentette be közleményben kedden az MTVA, amely azt is írta, hogy a közmédia arra törekszik, hogy az átmeneti időszak alatt is olyan médiát teremtsen, ami a társadalmi igényeknek is megfelel. Miután a 24.hu nyomán megírtuk, hogy Hajdú a Mészáros-csoportnál, Hír TV-nél, Echo TV-nél dolgozott, Magyar Péter hétfőn a cikk alá a Facebookon azt írta: „nem hinném…” Arról, hogy a miniszterelnök hogyan értette a kommentet, illetve a cikk mely részére reagált vele, érdeklődtünk hétfőn a Tisza Párt kommunikációjánál, de válasz ezen cikkünk megjelenéséig nem érkezett. A visszavonásról szóló cikkünk alá is kommentelt a miniszterelnök, azt írta: „Legyen sok eső! Hátha…” Hétfőn jelentette be a csatorna , hogy Hajdú Gábor lesz az M1 Híradó főszerkesztője, a műsor augusztus második felében tér vissza. Hajdú Gábor a Bessenyei György Tanárképző Főiskolán diplomázott, majd televízió- és filmproduceri oklevelet szerzett. Pályafutását 1997-ben a Magyar Televíziónál kezdte, ezt követően a Duna csatornánál járta be a teljes szakmai ranglétrát riporterként, tudósítóként és felelős szerkesztőként. 2015-től a Hír TV, majd az Echo TV munkatársa volt. A hétfői közlemény szerint az elmúlt években a vállalati kommunikáció és a társadalmi felelősségvállalás területén szerzett tapasztalatokat az üzleti és a civil szférában, de az MTVA a bejelentésben a Mészáros-csoportot nem említette, arról ezután a 24.hu írt. A közlemény akkor bejelentett két műsorvezetőt is. Az egyikük Borsa Miklós, aki ott volt a Híradó arcai között 2014-ben, majd visszavonult a tévézéstől. 2022-ben már kritikusan beszélt a köztévéről , ahol állítása szerint többször is olyat kellett beolvasnia, ami nem igaz, volt olyan is, hogy fegyelmit kapott, ha nem tette meg. Borsa megbízatását szintén visszavonták. A másik bejelentett műsorvezető Mészáros Szimonetta, ő korábban rádiós műsorvezetőként a Gong rádiónál és a Rádió Pápánál, hírolvasóként pedig a Hajdúszoboszlói Városi Televíziónál dolgozott. Közmédiás karrierjét 2024-ben a Nemzeti Sportrádió, majd a Petőfi rádió munkatársaként kezdte meg. A keddi, visszavonásról szóló közleményben őt nem említik. A közmédia átalakítását júliusban kezdték meg az MTVA új, ideiglenes vezetésével. Arról, hogy a hírszolgáltatások milyen ütemezés szerint indulnak újra, itt írtunk , arról pedig, hogy hogyan sötétült el a korábbi állami propagandacsatorna, itt olvashat . Kövess minket Facebookon is! Követem! Friss az Afteren

https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-airstrike-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JRlx Ukraine has increasingly targeted Russia's online retailers, destroying millions of square meters of warehouse space in recent weeks Image: Social Media/REUTERS Advertisement A Ukrainian airstrike killed nine people in Ukraine's eastern, Russian-occupied Luhansk region on Wednesday, according to Leonid Pasechnik, leader of Russia's occupying forces there. Pasechnik labeled the strike "a war crime," saying it had killed eight people on the spot and that another person, a 20-year-old woman, died of her injuries shortly thereafter. The bus was said to have been carrying 15 people, with five more reported injured. Ukraine keeps up strikes in Russia, destroys another major warehouse With US-brokered peace talks failing to get off the ground and the Kremlin sticking to its maximalist demands before agreeing to end its four-and-a-half-year invasion , Kyiv and Moscow have continued to escalate their air campaigns. Kyiv again targeted logistics infrastructure on Wednesday, using drones to destroy another Wildberries warehouse, this one in Russia's Tambov region, southeast of Moscow. Tambov's governor said the 100,000 square-meter (1.1 million square-foot) facility — an area roughly the size of 14 soccer fields — had been "completely destroyed by fire." Wildberries is Russia 's biggest online retailer. Ukrainian strikes on its facilities not only disrupt the Kremlin's military logistics — Kyiv says Wildberries aids the military war effort — they also strike at Russia's civilian economy and thus touch everyday Russians. This week, Kyiv expanded its target list to include Russia's number two online retailer, Ozon. In an analysis of satellite imagery, Reuters news agency estimated that at least 1.9 ​million square meters of warehouse space had been severely damaged in Ukrainian drone attacks on more than 20 Wildberries and Ozon facilities in recent weeks. Moscow: Ukraine launched hundreds of drones across Russia Sunday, killing at least six people in one of Kyiv's largest aerial attacks of the war. Kyiv has stepped up its attacks on Russia this year, with long-range missiles and swarms of drones increasingly targeting military industries and energy facilities. It has also increasingly pummeled giant Wildberries depots, burning billions of dollars' worth of merchandise belonging to the Russian online retail giant and bringing the war home to the Russian public nearly four-and-a-half years into Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Russia's Ministry of Defence said that it had destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight. Some 600 drones were detected headed toward the Russian capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, with a third of those destroyed over the Moscow region itself. An 83-year-old man was killed after a Ukrainian drone hit a private home in the Moscow region, local Gov. Andrey Vorobyov said. He also confirmed that a Ukrainian attack had sparked a blaze at a Wildberries warehouse in the town of Podolsk. A drone attack targeted three towns in Russia's southwestern Rostov region, killing five people, local Gov. Yury Slyusar said. The attack, with more than 150 drones, damaged several homes and a railway station and sparked a forest fire. Russian strikes kill 5 in Ukraine A Russian missile attack on Ukraine's Kryvyi Rih killed two people and wounded 14 others, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote on social media Sunday. He also said that one more person had been killed in the city of Sumy. Elsewhere, a man and a woman both died when their home was hit by a Russian strike in Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia region, said Ivan Fedorov, the head of the local military administration. More attacks sparked fires throughout the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, wounding six people.

"Wherever the Russians can reach with their ballistic missiles, they strike civilian infrastructure," Zelenskyy said. "Since this morning, air raid alerts have continued in many regions - the Russians launched another wave of drones." Russia's Ministry of Defence said Sunday that it had targeted a metallurgical plant in Kryvyi Rih and several military-industrial sites in Kyiv, including a manufacturing facility for Ukraine's Flamingo missiles. The domestically produced missiles are increasingly key to Ukraine's long-range attacks on Russia, with Zelenskyy announcing Saturday that Kyiv had used the weapons to attack a rocket research and production centre in Samara approximately 900 kilometres (560 miles) from the Ukrainian border. NATO jet downs drone in Romanian airspace Romania's Ministry of National Defence said Sunday that a Spanish Air and Space Force F-18 fighter jet shot down a drone that had entered Romanian airspace. The drone's entry into the NATO member's airspace was detected by surveillance systems at 4:44 am, the ministry said, about 24 kilometres (14.9 miles) north of the eastern city of Galati near the border with neighbouring Moldova. Moldova is a landlocked country between Ukraine and Romania. A Spanish F-18 aircraft that was performing air policing duties "made radar contact with the target and received engagement approval," the ministry said. "The drone was safely shot down by the F-18 aircraft at 05:01." Officials did not specify the drone's origin. The incident comes weeks after Romanian pilots shot down the three drones over three days from F-16 fighter jets, as Russia intensified attacks against Ukraine near the border. Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Romania has reported dozens of drone incidents, including some that have crashed and exploded on its territory. Acting Foreign Minister Oana Toiu said in a post on X that the Spanish deployment in Romania was scaled up "at the request of Romania and NATO to bolster the Eastern Flank following prior drone incidents," and that it was Spain's fourth such deployment.

Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images Republicans Republicans push back on Donald Trump’s wavering support for Ukraine GOP lawmakers threaten to pull support for president’s agenda after Russia diesel deal and sanctions pause US politics live – latest updates Ariana Baio in New York Tue 20 Oct 2026 13.32 EDT Last modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 14.59 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A handful of Republicans have spoken out against Donald Trump ’s softening stance on Russia , threatening to pull financial support for his agenda over his “embarrassing” handling of the Ukraine war. Don Bacon, an outgoing congressman in Nebraska, condemned Trump’s actions – which include a stunning agreement to buy Russian diesel and the pausing of sanctions on Moscow – as “absolutely disgraceful” and accused the US president of cozying up to a “war criminal” in Vladimir Putin, his Russian counterpart. “It really is disgraceful, and the Republicans that I associate with, there’s a lot of us, can’t stand it,” Bacon told CNN on Monday. “I think the president’s leverage in this Congress is shot.” US gave us no warning of Russian strikes on Kyiv power plants, Zelenskyy says Read more Last week, Trump waived sanctions imposed on Russia through a law named after his longtime ally and late senator Lindsey Graham. The legislation, which he signed only last month, was intended to increase financial pressure on Russia, more than four years after it invaded Ukraine. Instead, Trump announced he had struck a deal with Putin to import diesel fuel, which has become more expensive for Americans largely due to Trump’s war with Iran. Trump has previously blamed Ukraine’s strikes on Russia. Over the weekend, Trump claimed Ukraine’s president. Volodymyr Zelenskyy, “doesn’t care” about the impact of Ukraine’s strikes on Russia and “doesn’t want to end this war and probably never did” because Ukraine is receiving financial support from Europe. Trump also suggested Zelenskyy should step down on Monday, saying it was “time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine”. In an interview with Bloomberg , Zelenskyy said he believed Trump was taking steps to “convince Ukraine to capitulate” to Russian demands. On social media, Zelenskyy reaffirmed Ukraine’s partnership with the US . Darline Graham, the sister of Lindsey Graham and now a senator from South Carolina, broke with the president on his decision over the weekend, telling reporters on Saturday : “Personally, I would choose to put the pressure on Russia to end the war and get gas prices down because I don’t trust Putin, and I don’t trust Russia.” “[Ronald Reagan] and [Lindsey Graham] would be ashamed of this,” Bill Cassidy, the outgoing US senator from Louisiana, wrote on X in response to a recent Wall Street Journal editorial on the matter. Mitt Romney, a former Republican senator and presidential candidate, wrote on social media that if the US abandoned Ukraine, it would also “abandon liberty”. Some lawmakers had already raised concerns about the president’s support for Ukraine after Ukrainian officials said the country’s access to Starshield, a military version of the Starlink satellite internet service powered by Elon Musk’s company, was restricted last week . Musk hinted on social media that the US government controlled Ukraine’s access. Read more Brian Fitzpatrick, a Pennsylvania congressman, told MS Now on Monday that the Trump administration had not given “sufficient answers” about the recent disruptions to Starshield and the diesel deal. “This is wildly unacceptable, and it’s not going to stand,” Fitzpatrick said. “There’s going to be consequences to this. And by the way, it’s not just Starshield. It’s the diesel deal. It’s the lifting of sanctions. It’s all of this stuff.” Fitzpatrick said lawmakers would “demand accountability” and that they could take “punitive budgetary action” to force the administration to provide answers. Bacon told CNN he was unwilling to support the president’s agenda, such as building a triumphal arch or a new White House ballroom, while he withheld support for Ukraine. “Why would I want to support the president’s priorities, like the victory arch?” Bacon asked. “Frankly, what I see him doing here is surrendering.” Bacon added: “Why should we try to accommodate him and meet him halfway on funding when he is embarrassing this country so bad with what he’s doing with Putin and Zelensky?” Explore more on these topics Republicans Donald Trump Ukraine Russia Volodymyr Zelenskyy Vladimir Putin US foreign policy news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development
